question: What cumulative total of locally acquired dengue cases in Florida in 2026 will the FDOH Week 42 Arbovirus Surveillance Report show?

calls.reasoning: Week 40 report (Oct 4-10, published Oct 15) shows 368 cumulative; weekly adds were +62, +44, +72 in Weeks 38-40, and +40/wk on average from Week 35 to Week 37. Week 42 adds two more weeks (Weeks 41-42). Persistence at ~55-65/wk gives ~490. Upside: Pinellas emerging (37), first Brevard local case Oct 17, the record Week 40 jump. Downside: intensive mosquito control in Hillsborough, slightly cooler late-October weather, reporting lag. Fallback to a Week 41 report would still be >400, so no mass below 380. Market check: no Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold market found.
sources: https://www.floridahealth.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/fl-arbovirus-report-w41-2026.pdf (404, not yet published as of Oct 19)
calls.dossier:
- FDOH Week 40 report (Oct 4-10, published Oct 15, 2026): 368 cumulative 2026 locally acquired dengue cases in 8 counties: Broward 1, Hillsborough 310, Miami-Dade 9, Orange 5, Palm Beach 1, Pasco 4, Pinellas 37, Polk 1 (Yahoo/Tampa Bay summary; Outbreak News Today, ~Oct 16). Of 343 serotyped, 341 were DENV-2.
- Cumulative series: 41 (Week 33), 111 (Week 35), 190 (Week 37), 252 (Week 38), 296 (Week 39, week ending Oct 3), 368 (Week 40). Weekly adds: Week 38 +62, Week 39 +44, Week 40 +72 (record). Week 35 to Week 37 averaged ~40/wk.
- Hillsborough: 259 at Week 39, 310 at Week 40 (+51). Pinellas described as a 'new hotspot' (WINK News, Oct 15).
- Brevard County confirmed its first locally acquired case Friday Oct 17, 2026 (Hoodline/Fox35); likely counted in the Week 41 or Week 42 report.
- Hillsborough state of emergency extended through Oct 15; mosquito-control spending >$4M (Medical Daily). Whether it was extended again: not found.
- Expert quote (WINK, Oct 15): cases 'still seeing an increase'; spread to other counties via human movement.
- 2025 full-year Florida local dengue: 62 cases; 2026 is the largest mainland-US state total since the 1940s.
- Status quo: Week 42 total = 368 + Week 41 adds + Week 42 adds; the cumulative count does not decrease except through minor revisions.
- Resolves off the FDOH Week 42 report (week ending Oct 24, published ~Oct 29), 'Dengue Cases Acquired in Florida' year-to-date total; fallback is the latest report published by Oct 30 and dated after Week 40 (i.e., Week 41).
- Event window: 2026 YTD through the week ending Oct 24, 2026; as of Oct 19 the Week 41 period (Oct 11-17) is complete but unreported, and Week 42 (Oct 18-24) has just begun.
- Searched but not found: Week 41 report (404 as of Oct 19), onset-date epi curve, any prediction market (none on Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold).
calls.reference_class: Two-week increments of FDOH cumulative locally acquired dengue counts during the 2026 Florida outbreak (Week 35 to Week 40), plus past Florida outbreak seasonality (2024 Miami-Dade/Hillsborough peaks in Sep-Oct)

calls.reasoning: Week 40 (Oct 4-10) total is 368; Week 42 adds ~2 weeks. Recent weekly increments +62, +44, +72, with Pinellas nearly doubling (20->37) and a new county (Brevard) reporting a case; no sign of deceleration reported. Two weeks at ~50-80/week gives ~+110 to +165 -> median ~503. Downside: late-October cooling, vector control. Upside: geographic spread, reporting backlog. Market check: none found on Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold/bookmakers (Polymarket only tweeted news). >600 needs ~116/week (5%); <380 is implausible even via the Week 41 fallback.
sources: https://www.floridahealth.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/fl-arbovirus-report-w41-2026.pdf (404, not yet posted as of Oct 19)

- FDOH Week 40 report (Oct 4-10, 2026; published ~Oct 15): 368 locally acquired dengue cases YTD; +72 that week. Counties: Hillsborough 310, Pinellas 37, Miami-Dade 9, Orange 5, Pasco 4, plus Broward, Palm Beach, Polk (outbreaknewstoday; WUSF 2026-10-15).
- Of 343 serotyped, 341 are DENV-2, a single-serotype outbreak (outbreaknewstoday).
- Cumulative series: Wk33 41; Wk35 111; Wk37 190; Wk38 252; Wk39 (week ending Oct 3) 296; Wk40 368. Weekly increments: Wk38 +62, Wk39 +44, Wk40 +72.

- Brevard County announced its first locally acquired case ~Oct 16, 2026 (Fox35); may appear in Wk41/42 counts.
- Hillsborough and Pinellas emergency declarations extended through Oct 22; aerial and ground spraying ongoing; county mosquito spending >$4M (WUSF; MedicalDaily).
- One dengue death (80-year-old Tampa woman, Sept 4).

- Status quo: continued weekly accrual; the cumulative count cannot fall except via revisions (rare, small).
- Seasonal context: Tampa Bay Aedes activity typically declines as temperatures drop in Nov-Dec; late October is usually still warm enough for transmission. Past FL outbreaks (2023-2024 Miami-Dade) kept adding local cases into Nov-Dec.

- Event window: report covers YTD through Oct 24, 2026; as of Oct 19 about 5 of the remaining 14 days of accrual have elapsed (Week 41 ended Oct 17).

calls.reference_class: Linear extrapolation of the 2026 FL weekly local-dengue increments (Weeks 37-40), a large-outbreak growth phase, checked against prior Florida outbreaks (2024 Miami-Dade, 2023) where local cases kept accruing into November

Onset counts still rising (Aug 159, Sep 188), geographic spread to Pinellas (+17) and Brevard, Tampa still warm in late Oct → central +60-70/wk → ~500. Downside: intensive vector control, cooling, reporting saturation, small chance Week 41 fallback (~430). Upside: acceleration toward +100/wk. No prediction market found on Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold.
calls.dossier:
- FDOH Week 40 report (Oct 4-10, 2026; published ~Oct 15): 72 local dengue cases reported that week; 2026 cumulative 368 locally acquired cases, 8 counties: Hillsborough 310, Pinellas 37, Miami-Dade 9, Orange 5, Pasco 4, Palm Beach 1, Polk 1, plus Brevard (first case, news ~Oct 15-16). Onset months: July 21, Aug 159, Sep 188 (no Oct onsets listed yet → reporting lag). 341/343 serotyped DENV-2. Travel-associated: 26 in week 40, 288 YTD (source: FDOH W40 PDF as quoted by search snippet; Yahoo/Brevard article).
- Cumulative series per question background/news: W33 41, W35 111, W37 190 (W36 ~152 as of week ending Sep 12 per Medicaldaily/WFLA), W38 252, W39 296, W40 368. Weekly increments: ~+38/+40 (Sep), +62, +44, +72.
- WUSF Oct 15 2026: Hillsborough +51 in W40 (to 310), Pinellas +17 (20→37); both counties extended mosquito emergencies through Oct 22; 24/7 fogging, larviciding, contracted Clarke support; officials say true infections higher.
- Hillsborough 80-year-old Tampa woman died Sept 4 (first death).
- FDOH historic local dengue annual totals: 2020 77, 2021 0, 2022 68, 2023 199, 2024 93; 2025 ~40 by week 38. 2026 is record since 1940s.
- Status quo: cumulative only grows; W42 adds two report-weeks (W41, W42) to 368.
- Resolves off FDOH Week 42 report (week ending Oct 24, expected ~Oct 29) 'In 2026, N cases of locally acquired dengue' sentence, not news reports; fallback = latest report on/before Oct 30 dated after W40 (i.e., W41).
- Event window: cumulative through Week 42 (ending Oct 24, 2026); as of Oct 19 Week 41 underway (~5 of 14 days of accrual window elapsed); W41 report expected ~Oct 22 not yet published.
- Factors down: intensive vector control since Aug, late-Oct cooling, possible testing/reporting saturation. Factors up: onset counts rising month over month, spread to Pinellas/Brevard, report lag means Sept-Oct onsets still accruing.
- Searched, absent: Week 41 report (404 as of Oct 19); any Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold market on this; weekly onset epi curve detail.
calls.reference_class: Recent weekly increments of this same 2026 FDOH cumulative series (weeks 35-40), projected two weeks forward

calls.reasoning: Week 40 cumulative is 368; resolving Week 42 report adds two report-weeks. Recent weekly increments +38,+62,+44,+72 (mean ~54, rising trend); geographic spread (Pinellas 20->37, first Brevard case) pushes up; intensive vector control, late-Oct cooling, and modest onset growth (Aug 159 -> Sep 188) push down. Central ~+62/wk -> ~492. Fallback to Week 41 (~410-440) still above 380, so no lower escape. >600 needs ~116/wk, ~3%. No prediction market found per all runs.
calls.reconciliation: Runs agreed on all load-bearing facts (Week 40 = 368, increments +62/+44/+72, Week 41 not yet published, no market). Minor factual disputes (Broward vs Brevard as 8th county in W40; emergency extension through Oct 15 vs Oct 22) could not be checked without web access and do not move the estimate. The core dispute is judgment over the weekly rate for Weeks 41-42 (~55-65 vs 60-80). I weight the 4-week mean (~54) and the recent uptick and spread roughly equally against vector control and cooling, landing at ~+62/wk, median 492, and the 3% upper escape from Run 1, since 116+/wk has no precedent in the series.
